neighbours.label: subject pronoun that opens an emphatic or pseudo-cleft clause (What I ..., But we do ...): sets up emphatic 'do'
fire: The budget is tight this year. What we can do is delay the second phase.
I won't repeat the whole review here, but what I will say is that the food was superb.
Nobody expects miracles from the new manager. But they do expect some honesty.
The data are incomplete. What it shows, though, is a clear rise in cases.
Most of the plan was dropped. What they kept was the idea of a shared garden.
We can't change the weather. But we can change how we prepare for it.
He rarely talks about the war. What he does remember is the cold.
The rules are not perfect. But you do have to follow them while you are here.
quiet: The budget is tight this year. We plan to delay the second phase until spring.
I won't repeat the whole review here, and I think the food was superb.
Nobody expects miracles from the new manager, who starts work on Monday.
The data are incomplete. The report shows a clear rise in cases.
Most of the plan was dropped. The council kept the idea of a shared garden.
We can't change the weather, so the event moved indoors this year.
He rarely talks about the war, and his letters mention only the cold.
The rules are not perfect, and the staff explain them when visitors arrive.

notes: Card: peaks on ' I', ' we', ' they' after 'What' or 'But'; output promotes ' do', ' did', ' indeed', ' yes'. The - pole is the auxiliary itself (do/did/is).
